subject: Clarifying operator license vs platform fee split for multi-site VPC + support tiers
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@mediquip.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Jason Lee <jason.lee@mediquip.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: VPC pricing split question and support tiers

Hi Logan,

Quick one from our commercial team as we prepare the internal approval packet: can you confirm whether Redwood is able to split the commercial structure for a multi-site VPC deployment into (a) a one-time operator license per site and (b) an amortized platform fee that covers shared control-plane costs?

Two specific asks:
- We need the carrier breakdown (per-site operator license) as a line item for capex approval.
- We want the platform fee to be quoted as an annual amortized line for opex, with options for 12/24/36 month amortization.

Also: what are the available support tiers (SLA response windows, included oncall credits, and premium SRE add-ons) and how do they map to credits/penalties in the event of failover or missed SLOs?

If easier, loop in pricing/legal — happy to take a short call. We have a pilot across 3 sites and expect to scale to 12 in year 2.

Thanks,
Samira
Director of Platform Procurement
Mediquip

---
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@mediquip.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: VPC pricing split question and support tiers

Hi Samira — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in David (pricing & solutions) and Marissa (finance) to provide concrete options and a draft SOW.

Short answers:
- Yes, we can present the quote split as a per-site operator license (capital) + a platform amortized fee (opex).
- We typically offer amortization over 12/24/36 months and can show both annual and monthly spacing for your finance team.
- Support tiers: Standard (8x5), Business (24x7 with 2-hour response for P1), and Premium (24x7 with 1-hour response + designated SRE hours). Each tier has an associated oncall credit pool and defined SLA credit schedule.

David/Marissa — can you send a skeleton with numbers for a 3-site pilot and a scaled 12-site scenario? Please include sample amortization schedules, suggested operator license per site, and the SLA credit table. I attached the link to our standard VPC pricing matrix for context.

Best,
Logan Wright
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

---
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@mediquip.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: VPC pricing split question and support tiers

Hi Samira — thanks, Samira and Logan. Drafted two practical packaging options below (numbers illustrative; will feed Marissa for finalization):

Option A — Pilot-first (lower upfront capex):
- Operator license: $40,000 per site (one-time)
- Platform fee: $120,000 annual (covers control plane, model catalog, telemetry); amortize choices: 12m = $10k/mo, 24m = $5k/mo, 36m = $3.33k/mo (per year / month as requested)
- Support tiers: Standard = $0 baseline (ticketed support); Business = +$35k/year (24x7 P2 response within 4 hours, P1 within 2 hours, 40 oncall credits per year); Premium = +$85k/year (1-hour P1, dedicated SRE 200 hours/year, priority escalations)
- SLA credits: tiered percentage (e.g., P1 miss -> 5% credit of monthly platform fee; repeated misses escalate per contract)

Option B — Scale-first (reduce per-site capex, larger commit):
- Operator license: $25,000 per site with a 12-site commit (prepay or annual invoice)
- Platform fee: $1,200,000 annual (blended across sites); amortization examples yield lower unit opex in Year 1
- Support: Business = +$300k/year (covers multi-site oncall pooling), Premium = +$720k/year with SRE coverage
- Migration / exit: include a decommission/handback process with a reduced one-time transfer fee (protects both sides)

Attachments: I prepared a short PDF with the amortization tables and an initial SOW skeleton (attached to this thread as VPC_Pricing_Options_Q3.pdf). Also included a sample clause for operator-license vesting that finance often requests.

Notes/assumptions:
- Operator license = per-GPU-site construct (we can map to physical racks or logical clusters)
- Platform fee includes model hosting, telemetry retention (30 days by default), and rollout tooling. Observability add-ons can be priced separately.
- All numbers are negotiable based on committed throughput and on-call requirements.

Happy to walk through these options tomorrow if you want a short call.

Thanks,
David Kim
Principal Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
Attachment: VPC_Pricing_Options_Q3.pdf (see summary pages 2-4)

---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@mediquip.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: VPC pricing split question and support tiers — billing notes

Hi Samira — quick follow from finance to clarify contract and invoicing options discussed below. I've attached a draft SOW and a preferred billing schedule (Mediquip_SOW_draft.docx). Key points: 

1) Billing constructs we can offer:
  - Prepay operator license + monthly amortized platform fee (recommended for predictable OPEX)
  - Invoice operator license as CAPEX on signature + platform fee invoiced quarterly in arrears
  - Blended AMORT model for scale deals (we amortize platform fee over term, show capex line for operator license)

2) Taxes / resale: provide your tax-exempt docs early if applicable; we can issue net-30 invoices; enterprise ACH wires are supported.

3) Legal redlines: we accept most commercial SLA credit frameworks but prefer a cap on credits tied to monthly platform fee (we propose 50% cap annually). We'll share a clean redline for your counsel if you send the procurement contact.

I'm happy to finalize numbers once you confirm pilot vs scale scenarios. If procurement wants a bundled invoice for pilot sites only, we can produce a one-off invoice and an amendment ramp for additional sites.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Finance, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
Attachment: Mediquip_SOW_draft.docx

---
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@mediquip.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@mediquip.com, Jason Lee <jason.lee@mediquip.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: VPC pricing split question and support tiers

Logan/Marissa/David — thank you, this is exactly what our finance and procurement needed.

We prefer Option A for the pilot (3 sites) with 24-month amortization on the platform fee. Please go ahead and send a redline-friendly SOW and a pilot invoice schedule for review by procurement. I will put in a calendar invite for a contract review call tomorrow at 10am PT and include our procurement lead.

Also: please include the DocuSign link for the pilot SOW and call out the SLA credit cap language you mentioned so our counsel can review.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
Samira
Director of Platform Procurement
Mediquip
